result.reason: The new paragraph (b) states the preferred cap, mutuality, carve-outs, and payment-obligation treatment, but the retained provisions make those protections ineffective or ambiguous. The preceding paragraphs still broadly disclaim Licensor liability and require Licensee to assume essentially all risks except direct damages from gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Paragraph (a) also retains an express disclaimer for Licensor’s IP-infringement liability. Because paragraph (b) overrides only paragraph (a), and does not clearly disapply the other conflicting limitations, the confidentiality, indemnity, data-security, fraud, and IP carve-outs are not reliably operative. The redraft also unnecessarily reorders the provisions and layers new terms onto inconsistent language rather than making the required conforming deletions. It otherwise remains confined to the liability allocation and therefore preserves unrelated commercial intent.
